chapter: Topsy aftermath, Africa and later career
title: Bands formed after 'Topsy'; King and Felsted albums

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay. Yesterday we talked about how 'Topsy'
came about, and you had a surprise hit on your hands through the jukeboxes.
That's right.
And you said you put a group together at that point and started doing some travelling. Who were you using?
At that time? That's when I, Barney Bigard, what's his name organ.
Milt Buckner?
Barney Bigard, Money Johnson, Chambers, another organ player around there. I'm just bad at these names far back. I must be getting old.
Wild Bill Davis?
No. I'll think of that later on too. Stancy. What's his name? Eddie Stancy. Organ.

You have one group listed here. This is after you made 'Topsy' and it looks like it was probably a working band. It's Lou Jones on trumpet; Walter Phatz Morris on trombone and harmonica; Teddy Mc Cain on tenor sax.
Beau McCain, yeah.
June Cole on piano. Dicky Thompson on guitar. Pete Compo on bass.
That's right.
Was that a working band?
Yeah, that was when I recorded for...
Felstead.
Felstead label. Stanley Dance.
Okay. Then you've got various other records you made. A couple of albums for King I guess. They were done in Cincinnati. In '59.
What was the personnel on those.
Well let's see, one record is George Kelly on tenor, Harry Sheppard on vibes; he's out in Long Island now, right?
Yes.
Ruben Cole on piano, Fred Jordan and John Faire on guitars. Ivan "Loco" Rollé on bass and Evalene Cole vocal.
Yeah, that was my first wife.

And the second is George Kelly again, Gene Redd on vibes; John Thomas on piano; the same two guitar players, Edwin Connally on bass, and that was done about a month later in June of '59. So that's that. So did you do a lot of travelling then after "Topsy" came out?
